buildSourceNote: Build 148 carries v1.1.0-rc.25 - the two in-house pay verticals, and a finding that matters more than the feature. THE FEATURE: the owner ruled, verbatim, that technicians are all mechanics but electricians are different. src/lib/revenue-split-engine.ts now derives a binary vertical (verticalOfRole returns MECHANICS or ELECTRICAL) and, when BOTH are on a job, splits the labour 50/50 between them and then subdivides inside each by the existing ladder; when the TOTAL in-house headcount exceeds 4 the taper stops and each vertical divides its own half equally. A single-vertical job - the common case - is bit-for-bit unchanged, which is pinned by a regression test. The electrician test matches on elec rather than electrician on purpose: production employee 21 is spelled Jr. elecrician, and the longer substring would have silently paid them out of the wrong half. 25 tests pass, 11 of them new, including a money sweep asserting every mixed split still sums to the exact labour amount. CORROBORATION, and the reason this is not just an interpretation: the production table revenue_splits already held these rules as configured reference data - T1 100, T2 60/40, T1_E1 Technician 50 percent Electrician 50 percent. Both the 60/40 shipped in build 147 and the 50/50 across verticals here match a matrix that was already in the database. THE FINDING: THE SPLIT ENGINE HAS NEVER PRODUCED A SINGLE PRODUCTION SPLIT. Measured, not inferred - job_revenues 0 rows, job_revenue_split_details 0, job_revenue_split 0, job_technician_maps 1, job_card_technician 0, technician_productivity 0, technician_kpi_daily 0, productivity_alerts 0, and job_card_master has 671 rows with tech_slot_1 through tech_slot_5 empty on EVERY ONE. Not a single job card in production has a technician assigned. revenue_split_log holds 13 rows with real job cards and labour/spare amounts, but every derived column reads 0.00 and recorded_by is NULL - the log was written, the split never was. This CORRECTS an earlier claim in this build line that the runtime path uses job_technician_maps so splits ARE produced for new work and only the backfill was thin: that was wrong, nothing is produced. Consequence: neither the 60/40 of build 147 nor the vertical layer here changes any existing row, because no such row exists. The risk was never retroactive. ASSUMED, NOT VERIFIED, awaiting the owner: Wheel Alignment and Mechanical Helper both classify as MECHANICS; and with 3 mechanics plus 1 electrician the ladder gives the lone electrician 50 percent of the labour while each mechanic receives about 16.7 percent - implemented exactly as specified rather than quietly softened, but a large swing that may have been meant as headcount-weighted. STILL NOT IMPLEMENTABLE: the vendor/outsourced vertical. There is no vendor cost column anywhere in the schema, and job_technician_maps.employee_id carries a FOREIGN KEY to employees, so a non-employee vendor cannot be recorded on a job at all. GATES: lint:fabrication PASS; tsc --noEmit unchanged with the same 9 pre-existing errors, none in a file this build touches; 25 tests pass in the revenue-split suite. STILL OPEN FROM rc.24, NOT FIXED HERE: the served /version.json reports build 127 because it is copied from public/version.json, a different file with a different schema that no release step updates.
